title: In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts, stop a capacity refusal from burning the compose cooldown.
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts, stop a capacity refusal from burning the compose cooldown.

The file already establishes the governing principle at line 2061: "A compose that never RAN is not a compose that FAILED." The predicate isNonAttemptComposeResult (line 2082) already implements that test and already protects failed_attempts and category calibration from a BUSY result. The compose COOLDOWN was never given the same treatment, and that is the bug.

The cooldown is stamped at pick-start, before feature_compose runs, by this exact line:
  if (!pointer.gap_id && gap.id) gapComposeLastAttemptAt.set(String(gap.id), Date.now());
and it is read by this exact line:
  const eligible = gaps.filter((g) => nowMs - (gapComposeLastAttemptAt.get(String(g.id ?? "")) ?? 0) >= GAP_COMPOSE_COOLDOWN_MS);
with GAP_COMPOSE_COOLDOWN_MS = 300000.

Change: when the compose result is a non-attempt, clear that gap's cooldown stamp so the gap becomes immediately re-eligible for the auto-pick candidate set. Reuse the existing isNonAttemptComposeResult predicate — do not re-derive the BUSY / stage=capacity test. The natural site is the existing branch at line 3133 that reads `if (isNonAttemptComposeResult(cb)) {` and currently only logs "gap credit not bumped, category calibration untouched"; add the cooldown clear there, beside the log, so credit and selection are protected by one and the same decision.

Constraints that must hold after the change:
- A BUSY / stage=capacity result must still NOT bump failed_attempts and must still NOT touch category calibration. That accounting is correct today and must not regress.
- A genuine compose result — landed, or failed for a real reason — must STILL cool the gap for the full 5 minutes. Only the never-ran case is exempt.
- Do not change GAP_COMPOSE_COOLDOWN_MS, do not change COMPOSE_MAX_CONCURRENT, and do not change the slot cap or the directed-lane reservation.

Add a test asserting BOTH directions: a non-attempt result leaves the gap immediately re-pickable, and a real non-landing compose still cools it.

Why this matters, measured live on 2026-08-29: the autonomous lane has exactly one compose slot, composes run for many minutes, so most autonomous picks return BUSY. Each of those refusals cooled its gap for a full 5 minutes despite no compose having run. One gap was observed being picked at 19:26:31.9, 19:31:46.5, 19:36:52.6, 19:41:56.7 and 19:47:01.5 — deltas of almost exactly 5:00, cooldown-limited rather than tick-limited — and every one of those picks logged verdict=BUSY stage=capacity. Zero composes ran in that window for that gap.
